chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, concerning:
Regarding a well into which a dead animal falls, he said: “If it has an odor, twenty buckets are drawn from it.” And he said: “If the junub enters the well, seven buckets are drawn from it.”

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well; the water source under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةُ: a dead animal or carcass that contaminates the well
key_terms.رِيحٌ: odor or smell indicating stronger contamination
key_terms.سَبْعُ دِلَاءٍ: seven buckets; the specified amount to be drawn in the second case
key_terms.عِشْرُونَ دَلْوًا: twenty buckets; the specified amount to be drawn in one case
key_terms.نُزِحَ: water was drawn out; the prescribed method of removing water from the well

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a dead animal falls into a well or a junub enters it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings on purifying well water after contamination. It specifies a number of buckets to be drawn when a carcass falls into the well and has an odor, and when a junub enters the well, reflecting fiqh rulings on ritual purity and water purification.
